nodes.label: Flow Duration Curves and Afforestation
nodes.rationale: Journal of Hydrology 310 (2005), pages 253–265, DOI 10.1016/j.jhydrol.2005.01.006. Develops a method to separate rainfall variability from afforestation effects on streamflow.
nodes.author: Patrick N.J. Lane; Alice E. Best; Klaus Hickel; Lu Zhang

nodes.label: Flow Duration Curve
nodes.rationale: Represents streamflow against the proportion of time that flow is exceeded; annual deciles are derived from daily flows.

nodes.label: Rainfall Plantation Age Adjustment
nodes.rationale: Fits annual flow percentiles using rainfall deviation and a sigmoidal plantation-age term, then substitutes average rainfall to isolate vegetation effects without requiring paired catchment observations.

nodes.label: Ten Southern Hemisphere Catchments
nodes.rationale: Study dataset comprises catchments in southeastern Australia, South Africa, and New Zealand with diverse rainfall, soils, plantation species, and planted proportions.

nodes.label: Zero Flow Day Model
nodes.rationale: An inverse sigmoidal model characterizes increased stream intermittence at Stewarts Creek, Pine Creek, and Redhill; the paper cautions that these small, extensively afforested catchments may represent maximum effects.

nodes.label: Afforestation Response Groups
nodes.rationale: Group 1 has larger low-flow reductions and more zero-flow days; Group 2 has more uniform proportional reductions. Storage differences are proposed as a partial explanation, not established as a measured causal result.

nodes.label: Nash Sutcliffe Model Efficiency
nodes.rationale: Evaluates observed versus modeled flow percentiles and zero-flow days. The authors treat efficiency above 0.7 as adequate and report weaker fits at several low-flow percentiles and Lambrechtsbos sites.
